title: I built a fast-paced survival FPS with AI — and a platform to host games like it
author: Ok-Dependent6772
selftext:
I've been experimenting with AI-assisted game development and wanted to share one of the projects I've been working on.

Hellspawn: a fast-paced retro survival shooter where you fight increasingly difficult waves of enemies, unlock new areas and weapons, upgrade your character, and try to push your high score as far as possible.

I've been using AI heavily throughout development — especially for coding, iteration, debugging, gameplay systems, assets, and rapidly testing ideas that I probably wouldn't have attempted otherwise.

HELLSPAWN is also running on [**3js.games**](http://3js.games), a platform I'm building for small browser games and experimental web experiences. The idea is to make it easy for developers to publish HTML5/WebGL games while giving them things like leaderboards, cloud saves, player identity, profiles and discovery without having to build all of that infrastructure themselves.

I've included a short video of HELLSPAWN in the post.

I'm especially curious what other AI game developers think about this workflow. Do you think platforms specifically built around small AI-assisted/indie web games could be useful, or would you rather just host games independently?

HELLSPAWN: [https://www.3js.games/games/hellspawn](https://www.3js.games/games/hellspawn)  
Platform: [https://www.3js.games/](https://www.3js.games/)

comments.author: IllustriousTip6904
comments.body: Whatd you use for the assets?

replies.author: Ok-Dependent6772
replies.body:
For the visual assets I mostly used OpenAI Image 2.0.

I first created a small moodboard/style reference to lock down the overall look, then generated a larger batch of candidate assets through the OpenAI API. From there I manually curated the images that fit the game best.

After that I used Codex to process and integrate them into the game, things like preparing the files, handling transparency/cropping where needed, naming assets consistently, wiring them into the project, and adapting them to the low-res/retro rendering style.

For the audio i found a sample of different zombie sounds and got Codex to work, took almost no time for it to create time markers and splitting the audio. The rest of the audio was scattered around numerous sample packs (used to produce music), gave the sounds fitting names and made Codex integrate it where they fit.
